mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -2% AND HOUST falls for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS rising YoY for four consecutive months) signals a shift from consumption to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth > 0% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 100,000 jobs signals labor market weakness, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls by > 100,000 in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both industrial production (INDPRO) and the housing starts index (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a broad-based supply-side expansion, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
